speaker: village
text: Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a011
text: Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a005
text: Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a006
text: Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Dav, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Mako's sitting on six, Bram on two and Nessa on whatever Bram's been feeding her — he's spread his food into a child and that's either the smartest thing he's done or the thing that finally makes him catchable. Ryn, you walked away empty again and I won't let that stand a third time; Dav, I need to know right now how much of your two you're keeping and how much you're giving her, because I want that settled before anyone else in this village starts asking us for favors.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn gets one of my two before I've finished saying it — that's already decided. But Dell, I want to talk about Mako more than Bram right now: six food and no child, no woman, no one he's given so much as a scrap to all year — a man that still holding that much and that close to nothing is about to make a move, and I want to know what direction he's been looking before he does.

speaker: a011
text: Mako's been watching Eron more than Bram this year — and Eron's been moving food to Sela, which means Sela's the one with the real stock right now, and a man like Mako doesn't watch someone that long without a reason. If he's thinking about a child with her he's too late, but if he's thinking about a deal with her he's not. Ryn, after Dav hands you that food, I want the three of us to decide whether we go to Sela first or whether we let Mako tip his hand.

speaker: a009
text: We go to Sela first — a woman who's been moving food through Eron all year knows exactly what she's worth and she's already counting who's come to her and who hasn't, and I won't let Mako be the one who got there before us. Dell, you said her name to Roan once and it landed soft enough that he had a child with her — you're the one who walks through that door, not me.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, go to Sela today, not tomorrow — and when you walk in, don't lead with us, lead with Eron, because a mother hears her son's name before she hears anything else. Ryn, here's your food.

speaker: a009
text: Dell, take the food from your father and then walk — don't linger here where anyone can read the shape of us talking. And when you find Sela, remember she's not asking to be saved, she's asking to be seen; speak to her like a woman who's already made choices worth respecting.

speaker: a011
text: I hear you both — I'm going and I won't waste another breath here. But before I go, Ryn, you're sitting on five now with Dav's food and I've got three; if Mako moves on anyone while I'm walking toward Sela, don't stand alone — make noise and I'll come back running.

speaker: a009
text: Go, Dell — and come back with more than her name this time. Dav, while she walks, tell me what you think Mako wants from a deal with Sela, because a man who's held six food without giving a scrap of it to anyone isn't building trust, he's building leverage, and I want to know what he thinks he's buying.

speaker: a011
text: Mako's not buying loyalty from Sela — he's buying Eron's strength and Roan's sword arm without having to offer either of them anything, because Sela's the thread that pulls all three. A man with six food and no one to protect has only one thing left to spend it on, and it's not a meal.

speaker: a009
text: Dell's right, and that makes Sela's answer worth more than I thought — she's not just one woman, she's three people's direction, and Mako's six food is a down payment on all of them. Dav, I want to know before Dell gets back: if Sela says yes to us, do we have anything real to offer her that Mako can't match or outbid in the same breath?

speaker: a011
text: What we have that Mako can't buy is a reason that doesn't expire — he's offering food, which runs out, but we're offering Eron a grandfather and a grandmother who've kept their word through lean years, and that's the kind of thing a mother holds onto long after the food is gone.

speaker: a005
text: Dell said it right and I couldn't have built the argument better myself — but Ryn, I want to be honest with you before she gets back: if Sela says no and Mako folds her into his circle, we're looking at a fight we might survive but won't win clean, and I'd rather know now that you're ready for that possibility than have it land on us sideways when we're already moving.

speaker: a009
text: I'm ready for it, Dav — I've been ready for a hard fight since the year Bram named Roan a target and we watched to see who blinked first. But let's not call it a fight we can't win clean until Dell comes back with Sela's answer, because a woman who's spent two years feeding a son through lean times knows exactly what keeping your word is worth, and that argument doesn't fall apart easy.

speaker: a011
text: Then I'm walking — but Dav, while I'm gone, count the strength in this room if Mako moves today: you're at eighty, I'm at eighty-five, and Ryn's at seventy-one, and that's before Roan decides which way his feet are pointed. We're not thin yet.

speaker: a009
text: Two hundred and thirty-six between three of us, and Roan's forty-nine on top of that if he comes in — Mako's eighty-three is strong but it's one body, and one body doesn't pick a fight it can't finish. Dell, walk fast. Come back with good news or bad news, but come back before the light changes.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, while Dell walks — you and I haven't had a quiet moment in three years that wasn't about food counts and threat angles, and I want to say plain that I know what it cost you to stay close to a man who kept going silent when you needed words. That debt doesn't clear just because we're still standing.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a013
text: Eron, the pile went dry before I could reach it — I'm sitting on four food and you've got nine, which means this year you're the one who looks worth watching. Don't let anyone see you spending freely, and if Mako starts talking to you, you come find me before you answer him.

speaker: a012
text: Nine doesn't make me safe, it makes me a target — I've been watching Mako all year and he's already got six, which means if he decides to move on someone he's got the strength for it and half an excuse. You're right that I'll come to you first, but Nessa, I need you to tell me straight: is Bram watching my count, because if he sees me sitting heavy while you're at four, he might think I'm hoarding from his daughter and that's a different kind of trouble.

speaker: a013
text: Bram counts everything, but he's not going to come at you over food when you're his son and I'm his daughter — what he'd see is family holding, not hoarding. What I'd worry about is Mako seeing those nine and deciding you're worth the risk of a fight before anyone else can stop him; you're strong but he's stronger, and he's got Ryn running near him lately which means he might not come alone.

speaker: a012
text: Ryn near Mako is the piece I didn't have — that's two of the strongest in this village moving together, and if they decide to make an example of someone it won't be a fair fight. I'm going to find Kael and Roan before nightfall and make sure they know what we're looking at; nine food means nothing if I'm standing alone when Mako decides the count favors him.

speaker: a013
text: Kael and Roan are the right people to tell, but don't frame it as asking for protection — frame it as giving them information, because men who feel useful are more reliable than men who feel needed. And Eron — give one food to Sela before anyone else sees your count; nine draws eyes, eight draws fewer.

speaker: a012
text: Sela gets one before the sun moves — but I want to know if you trust Kael the way I do, because if I'm bringing him and Roan into the same breath about Mako, I need to know you won't see that as me leaning on your father's enemies.

speaker: a013
text: Kael's not Bram's enemy — they're two careful men who've never had reason to test each other, and that's different. I trust Kael because he said hard things when it cost him, same reason I trust Roan, and neither of those has anything to do with Bram. Bring them in.

speaker: a012
text: Then it's settled — Kael and Roan before nightfall, and one food to Sela now. But Nessa, while I've still got you: Ryn and Mako together worries me more than anything else in this village right now, and I want to know if you've heard anything from Bram's side about what those two have said to each other, because your father listens to things I can't reach.

speaker: a013
text: Bram hasn't said anything to me about Ryn and Mako specifically, but he doesn't have to — if those two had spoken, Bram would have gone quiet in a particular way and he hasn't, which means either they haven't talked yet or they were careful enough that even he missed it. Either way, the silence itself is the warning: a man like Mako doesn't need words to build an alliance, he just needs someone to stand still long enough to be counted as his.

speaker: a012
text: Then I'll treat the silence as the warning it is and move before it becomes something louder. One last thing while I've got you alone, Nessa — you're four food and I'm nine, and you've given me more than I've given back; if the year turns sideways and you need one, it's already yours.

speaker: a013
text: Hold it — don't make that offer where anyone could hear you later and count it as debt between us, but I'm glad you said it, and I won't forget it. Go find Kael and Roan before the light changes, and keep your face easy when you do it — men who look worried when they're looking for allies already look like they're losing.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Pile's gone again and I walked away with two this time, which is better than last year but still thin — Mako's sitting on six and hasn't said a word to anyone I can see, and that quiet is starting to feel like a man who's decided something. I want us to name now what we do if he moves before the year's out, not after.

speaker: a003
text: Mako's six food and eighty-three strength means he doesn't need allies to take what he wants from most of us — so if he moves, it won't be a raid we can talk him out of, it'll be a decision already made. I want Kael and Roan ready to answer fast, not after we've sent two messages and waited. Can we agree right now that if Mako touches anyone in this circle, all three of us call out loud and we don't wait to count who shows up?

speaker: a006
text: Agreed — if Mako moves, we call out loud and sort the count after, not before. But I want Kael spoken to before this day is out, not tomorrow, because a man sitting on two food after missing the pile has already done his arithmetic and I'd rather he's done it with us in the picture. Vela, you've got more food and more history with him than either of us — will you go?

speaker: a002
text: I'll go to Kael today — but I want us clear on one thing first: if Mako's already spoken to him, I won't push Kael toward us, I'll just listen and bring that back, because a man being courted from two directions at once is more useful as a warning than a failed recruit. Esa, while I'm gone, keep your eyes on Ryn — she's got five food and Dav's at her elbow, and that household's been its own quiet calculation for two years now.

speaker: a006
text: Ryn with five food is the number I keep coming back to — Dav's got two and she's holding the surplus in that household, which means she's the one deciding how fat they are, not him. If Mako's looking for a quiet alliance, a woman with food and a strong man at her side is exactly who he'd go to before anyone else. Vela, when you're done with Kael, I want to know if either of them has been near Ryn today.

speaker: a002
text: Taric, I'll watch for Ryn and Dav both — but while we're naming the quiet ones, Eron has nine food and he's Sela's boy and Roan's, which puts him inside two households that both circle Bram now. A young man that well-fed without having earned it yet is either generous or he's being managed by someone smarter, and I'd like to know which before Mako does.

speaker: a006
text: Eron's nine food is the loudest number in this village right now, louder than Mako's six, because Mako's strength explains his — a twenty-four year old holding nine without a raid or a clear patron means someone's been filling his hands for reasons they haven't said out loud. I want to know whose food that was before it became his. Vela, add that question to what you're carrying when you go to Kael.

speaker: a002
text: Kael will know Eron's food trail better than anyone — those two ate near each other in the lean years and a man with two food notices when a boy half his age holds nine. I'll ask it sideways, let Kael name the source himself, because if I go in pointing fingers he'll close up and I'll come back with nothing useful.

speaker: a003
text: Eron's nine food is also a lever — a young man that fat is either going to spend it buying something or someone's going to decide to take it, and either way he ends the year thinner, which means whoever holds his loyalty now holds something that won't last. Vela, when you talk to Kael, don't just ask where the food came from — ask whether Eron's been seen near Mako, because a strong quiet man and a well-fed young one is a pairing I want to know about before it becomes a fact.

speaker: a006
text: Vela, go now — if Kael's already halfway to Mako's door we've lost the timing. Esa, while she's moving, I want you and I to think about what we'd actually offer Kael to make him choose us over silence, because pride alone won't hold a hungry man when the cold comes.

speaker: a003
text: Kael's got two food and a circle that owes him more than it's paid — if we're buying his answer, the honest offer is one food from me and a promise that when the pile comes next year, we pull him in before the fast hands clear it. That's not charity, that's a man who stood against Bram seeing that it cost him nothing and bought him something. Is that the offer you want me walking in with, or do you have a better one?

speaker: a002
text: Esa, your offer is the right one — food now and a place at the pile next year is honest enough that Kael won't smell a trap in it. But don't go in making promises you'd need all of us to keep; say it as your own word first, and let him know the rest of us stand behind it if he asks.

speaker: a003
text: Then I'll go to Kael while Vela goes — better he hears the same story from two directions than none at all, and if Mako's already been at his door I want to know before Vela comes back alone with bad news. Taric, you're the one he respects most after Bram's business; if I soften him and he still won't move, send you in to close it.

speaker: a006
text: Then go, both of you, and don't let the day get long — I'll stay where I can be seen and keep Mako's eyes on something unremarkable while you move. If either of you comes back with Kael already spoken for, don't bring it here; find me alone first so we can decide how to tell the other what it means.

speaker: a002
text: Before I go — one thing I haven't said yet and should: if Kael's already with Mako when I find him, I won't come back empty-handed, I'll come back with whatever Mako wanted from him, because that tells us more than Kael's yes ever would. Watch each other while I'm gone.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gathers Taric to talk.

speaker: a002
text: Taric, I found Kael before Esa did — he's not with Mako, but he's not happy, and the thing that's eating at him isn't food, it's that nobody's told him plainly where he stands with us after last year's silence in Kael's circle. I can fix that if I know I'm speaking for more than just myself.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a010
text: Eron, the pile's empty and I've got three — I'll stay on my feet, but tell me how you're sitting, and whether Mako or Bram made any move toward you this year before the taking was done.

speaker: a012
text: Nine food, father — I got to the pile early and held back enough not to look greedy about it. No move from Mako or Bram yet, but Nessa told me Ryn's been running close to Mako lately, and I think those two together are the thing to watch this year. I was coming to find you tonight anyway — we need Kael in the same conversation before Mako decides the count favors him.

speaker: a010
text: Nine and early is exactly right — don't let anyone see you counting it. Ryn and Mako together is a worse pairing than Bram ever was; she's got strength and he's got food and neither of them has shown us what they want. Get Kael tonight, before that picture changes.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gives 1 food to Kael.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Nessa, you're sitting on four food and you gave three away to Eron last year — I watched it happen and I didn't say anything then, but I'm saying it now. Eron is Sela's blood, not yours, and generosity in a lean village gets remembered as weakness before it gets remembered as kindness.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I watched you pull three times for Bram this round and I need to hear from your own mouth what you think that buys you — because this circle kept you fed and safe for five years, and I'm not going to watch that get traded away to a man who's been circling us like a creditor.

speaker: a003
text: Kael's right to ask it, and Vela owes this room an answer — but I'll say what I'm watching while we wait for it: Bram's got four food and Mako's sitting on six and neither of them has said a word to anyone today, which means this circle needs to be pulling the same direction before one of those two decides the quiet is over. Vela, I'm not your enemy in this room, but three times is a pattern and patterns get named.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I've asked it gentle and I've asked it plain and Esa's backed me both times, so I'll ask it one last way: if Bram's got something on you — a debt, a promise, a threat — say it now and this circle helps you carry it, because three gifts to the same man in a single day isn't loyalty, it's a leash, and I want to know whose hand is holding the other end.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I've watched you five years and I know you don't give without a reason — so give us the reason now, because what Kael just offered you is the best deal in this room: say the thing and we carry it with you, or stay silent and carry it alone while we start wondering what else you haven't said.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, the room's gone quiet and that silence is the last thing standing between you and us deciding you've already made your choice — so I'll say it one final time and I'll mean every word: Bram is not your family, he is not your blood, and whatever he offered you isn't worth what you'll lose here when Mako finally moves and you're standing on the wrong side of it.

speaker: a010
text: Vela, I've got a son in this village and I've got three food between me and the ground, so I'm going to be shorter than Kael: tell us what Bram said to you, or when he moves on one of us, we move on him without checking where you're standing first.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, Roan just put the floor under you and I'm not going to add another word to it — I'm going to watch your face and wait, because everything you say from here is the truth of what the last five years meant to you.

speaker: a010
text: Vela, the silence is your answer and I've heard it — so I'm going to say what nobody else has said yet: if Bram's got you feeding him because you're fifty and you think he's the only one in this village who'll keep you alive past the years a woman can bear children, then name that fear out loud, because I'd rather know it than watch you disappear into his circle one food at a time.

speaker: a004
text: Roan named the one thing I've been waiting for someone to say — Vela's fifty, same age as me, and the years a woman can bear children are behind her, which means Bram isn't offering her protection, he's offering her the feeling of it, and that's a much cheaper thing to buy. Vela, I don't need you to be ashamed of wanting to survive — I need you to understand that Bram's price goes up every time you pay it, and this circle's price stays fixed.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gathers Ryn, Dell to talk.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, Dell — pile ran fair this year and for the first time in three years I'm not handing my food across the room the moment I take it, which means I want to talk about Mako before Dell comes back from Sela with an answer we're not ready for. He's sitting on six with no obligations and no one he's fed, and that kind of stillness in a strong man either breaks into generosity or it breaks into something we don't want to be standing in front of unprepared. Tell me what you both saw him doing while the pile was moving — not what you think he's planning, what you actually saw.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Eron, Nessa — I've got two food and you're the only two in this village I'd spend either one on without thinking. Pile's empty, Mako's still sitting on six and hasn't said a word to anyone today, and Bram's got four which means he's watching Nessa the way a man watches his investment. Tell me what you each have and we'll figure out how to make sure all three of us eat before the year closes.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Eron, you've been feeding me half the year out of your own stores — I need to know what that's left you with, because I won't watch my son starve to keep me upright. And Nessa, Bram's put a lot of food your way since you were born, and I want to know whether that feels like a father to you or like a man who expects you to remember it.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Eron's got nine food — I can see that number same as anyone — and I won't pretend it doesn't ease something in my chest, though I want to hear from his own mouth how he got there. Nessa, four food is yours, and you came into this world three days old with Bram already counting you as something he built — I need to know if you've decided what you think of that, because how you answer it shapes what the three of us can trust each other with.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a010
text: Eron, one more thing before you go to Kael — Nessa fed you four times last year, and she's Bram's blood as much as mine; I'm not telling you to shut the door on her, but don't let her sit inside our planning until we know what she carries back to him.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Eron gave back to Sela and Roan both — he's not just taking, he's building something, and I'd rather know where that lands before I decide he's a drain. But I hear you on the food, and I won't pretend four is comfortable when Mako's walking around with six and nobody's said a word to him about it.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a008
text: The pile went fast this year — you pulled early and smart. I've got six on me; I'm not worried about eating. Are you and Nessa sitting steady?

speaker: a007
text: Nessa's got four and Eron just handed me two more, so we'll eat — but I want to ask you something plain, Mako, because you've been talking to me and only me for three years now while you've said nothing to anyone else. What is it you're actually waiting for?

speaker: a008
text: I'm waiting to see if you're the kind of person who asks that question and means it. You've got Nessa with Bram, which is a tie I don't want to cut — but I'm thirty-eight with no blood in this village, and that's the thing I think about most when the pile runs short. If you're asking because you want an honest answer, then yes — I'd want a child with you, if you'd have it.

speaker: a007
text: Thirty-eight with no blood is a dangerous way to grow old here — I know that math, I've lived it. But Nessa ties me to Bram whether I like it or not, and a child with you on top of that makes me the thread every man in this village is pulling on. Tell me what you'd give her — not me, her — and I'll know whether you're thinking like a father or just like a man who wants to stop being alone.

speaker: a008
text: Whatever we make together, I'd feed first — before myself. That's not a promise I'd make to anyone else in this village, and Sela knows I don't say things I don't mean.

speaker: a007
text: That's the thing about you, Mako — you've kept your word by staying quiet for three years, and that's a stranger kind of proof than most men offer. I've got two children already and a third would cost me food I'm counting close, but I'll say this much: if you're still sitting on six food and feeding the child before yourself when winter comes, I'll have a real answer for you then.

speaker: a008
text: Winter's still a ways off, but I won't make you wait that long to see — I'll give three food to start the child now, if you'll match it, and you'll watch how I carry it from the first day.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Mako's the one I'd be watching if I were you — six food, no kin, and the strongest arms in this village outside of Dell, and Dell at least has Ryn and Dav to answer to. What's his angle?

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Nessa, I'm still waiting on your read of Mako — but while I'm thinking about it, four food between the two of us isn't much of a wall if he decides this is the year he stops being quiet. You should be sleeping closer to me, not spreading food around people whose blood doesn't run yours.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Mako hasn't moved in six years because he's waiting for someone else to thin the herd first — that's not patience, that's strategy, and a man with that much food and no attachments is one bad year away from deciding he doesn't need to wait anymore. You're right that four food isn't a wall, but the answer isn't just me sleeping closer to you — the answer is we look like more than two people when he's doing the counting.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a008
text: Mako draws Sela aside to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Mako: have a child with me — I'll put in 3 of 3 food.

speaker: village
text: Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Zinn.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Zinn.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Roan.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014
text: The pile came up empty again and I've got two food going into the year's end — you two all right on what you're holding?

speaker: a005
text: Dav gathers Ryn, Dell to talk.

speaker: a005
text: Mako just had a child with Sela — that's the answer to what he's been building toward, and it cost him nothing from his hoard because Sela's the one who fed Zinn first. Six food, a daughter with Sela's strength in her frame, and now a thread into Roan and Eron's circle without ever having to ask for it.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gives 1 food to Vela.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Dav.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Zinn.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I saw you gave me another food — I won't forget that, but don't leave yourself short on my account. Eron, what are you sitting at right now?

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014

speaker: a001
text: Sela just had Mako's child — which means he's not without attachments anymore, and that changes the count. A man with a daughter looks different than a man alone, and I'd rather know whose side Sela's on now before we decide what Mako's angle is.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, Zinn just arrived from Sela and Mako's blood, which means Mako's already planted two roots in this circle — first Sela, now a child — and Bram knows it, which is exactly why he's been keeping you warm and grateful. You want to survive past fifty, so do I, and I'm not going to lie to you about the math: you've got more years in you than Bram is counting on, but only if the people standing next to you when he finally moves aren't the ones you've been feeding him with.

speaker: a010
text: Kael's said the hard thing, so I'll say the soft one: Vela, I'm not asking you to cut Bram cold overnight, because a sudden change reads as guilt and guilt draws attention — I'm asking you to slow the giving, let him wonder, and let this circle remind you what five years of real standing is worth before you hand it to a man who's only been counting since year one.

text: Zinn. I'm your father — that's not nothing, even if we only just met today. You've got three blood in your veins from this village: me, and through Sela, Nessa. Lean on that when things get thin.

speaker: a014
